questions.question: The distance between the points (3, 4) and (6, 8) is:
The midpoint of the segment joining (−3, 5) and (7, −1) is:
The point dividing the segment from A(2, 3) to B(8, 12) internally in the ratio 2 : 1 is:
The slope of the line through (2, 1) and (6, 9) is:
questions.rationale: m = (9 − 1)/(6 − 2) = 8/4 = 2; the line climbs 2 units for every 1 unit across.

questions.question: A line perpendicular to y = 3x + 4 must have slope:
questions.rationale: Perpendicular lines have slopes whose product is −1, so m = −1/3 (the negative reciprocal of 3).

questions.question: The slope of the line 2x + 3y + 6 = 0 is:
questions.rationale: In the general form ax + by + c = 0 the slope is −a/b, here −2/3.

questions.question: The area of the triangle with vertices (0, 0), (4, 0), and (4, 3) is:
questions.rationale: Base 4 and height 3 give ½ × 4 × 3 = 6; the shoelace formula returns the same ½|12| = 6.

questions.question: The triangle with vertices A(1, 2), B(4, 6), C(7, 2) is:
questions.rationale: AB = BC = 5 while AC = 6, so exactly two sides are equal — isosceles.

questions.question: If two distinct lines are parallel, their slopes:
questions.rationale: Parallel lines rise at the same rate, so their slopes are equal; slopes multiplying to −1 signals perpendicular lines.

questions.question: The distance of the point (3, 4) from the origin is:
questions.rationale: d = √(3² + 4²) = √25 = 5 — the classic 3-4-5 right triangle with the origin as the right-angle vertex.
